issue: Must the government prove intent to defraud as an element of a 18 U.S.C. § 912 impersonation offense, even though Congress removed that language in 1948?

sides.position: Intent to defraud remains an essential element of a § 912 violation, despite its removal from the statute in 1948.
cases: United States v. Gayle, 967 F.2d 483 (11th Cir. 1992)

sides.position: Intent to defraud is not a separate element of a § 912 violation, so the government need not prove it (the implied position the 1st Circuit does not adopt or reject here).
cases: United States v. Vazquez-Rosario, 45 F.4th 565 (1st Cir. 2022)

quote: Specifically, he argues the "intent to defraud" remains an inherent part of a § 912 violation which the government must prove, despite the removal of that language by Congress in 1948, a position which is supported by some of our sister circuits.
cite: United States v. Vazquez-Rosario, 45 F.4th 565 (1st Cir. 2022)
